behavior_in_task_description.explanation: This is a visual_bug_fix task whose entire spec is the annotated screenshot; instruction.md explicitly states 'the annotated screenshot ... is the whole report: everything that is wrong is marked on it, and the notes say what each marked thing does.' Cross-checking the screenshot's handwritten annotations against the f2p test list shows every tested defect is depicted: the two Optional +Add buttons funneling into the general section and the general +Add opening a Critter Power sheet (write-path tests), the two Optional sections holding each other's powers (read-path/bucketing test), the enable/disable control appearing on the wrong rows (toggle-visibility test), and the toggle flipping the section but leaving the wrong enabled flag (toggle-consistency test). No test checks a behavior that is absent from the screenshot's markings.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Every defect marked in the screenshot maps to a corresponding f2p test in tests/test_sprite_power_sections.mjs: mis-tagged section creation, general-section wrong item type, swapped optional-section rendering, and the toggle's section/enabled-flag mismatch are all explicitly asserted with named test cases and clear failure messages. p2p tests additionally guard the general 'must keep working' behaviors instruction.md alludes to (generic item creation, inventory unhide/select, non-power/non-optional toggle no-ops).

informative_test_structure.explanation: test_sprite_power_sections.mjs is heavily commented with a file-level docstring explaining the write/read/toggle round-trip methodology, section banners separating f2p vs p2p blocks, and a one-to-two line comment above every individual test case explaining exactly what behavior it targets and why. test.sh also documents each phase (patch apply, dep install, test run, reward computation) with inline comments.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The Dockerfile clones the real upstream repo, applies the bug patches, then strips .git entirely so the agent cannot inspect the future fix commit or PR history; the bug patches themselves are copied to /tmp (never into environment/assets, which is the agent-visible evidence dir) so their reverse-diffs never leak into the image. tests/ and solution/ are not copied into the image at all (confirmed absent from the Dockerfile COPY instructions) and are supplied only at verify time. The agent's network_mode is 'no-network', preventing it from fetching the real GitHub issue/PR (whose numbers are known) to read the actual fix. task.toml's detailed difficulty_explanation (which would give away all 6 defects) is harness-only metadata, never shipped to the container.

structured_data_schema.explanation: This is a source-code bug-fix task graded by rendering templates and driving existing TypeScript entry points; it does not require the agent to produce any structured data output (JSON/CSV/API schema), so this criterion does not apply.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The test-only Handlebars dependency is installed at verify time pinned to an exact version (handlebars@4.7.8) via --no-save so it never touches package.json. The TypeScript compiler is the repo's own pre-existing pinned devDependency, installed via `npm install` against the cloned repo's own package-lock.json. verifier.py uses only Python stdlib (no unpinned pip packages). apt packages (git, patch, ca-certificates, curl) are unpinned, which is acceptable per the criteria.

typos.explanation: Reviewed instruction.md, task.toml, all four bug patches, solution/fix.patch, solve.sh, test.sh, config.json, test.patch, and verifier.py; filenames consistently describe their patch content (e.g. bug_02_can_be_disabled_predicate.patch modifies canBeDisabled()), and no misspellings or broken paths/commands were found.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile only COPYs bugs/ (to a temp path, later removed) and assets/ (to /app/.harbor_assets/); it never copies tests/ or solution/, and this is explicitly called out in Dockerfile comments ('tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image -- the harness supplies them at verify time').

test_deps_in_image.explanation: Handlebars, the only genuinely test-only dependency (used solely by the verifier to render the candidate's templates), is installed in tests/test.sh at verify time with --no-save, not baked into the Dockerfile. The Dockerfile explicitly comments on this separation. TypeScript is left in the image build because it is a real build-time dependency of the cloned repository itself, not test-only.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solution/solve.sh applies solution/fix.patch, which is the genuine multi-file code diff (TypeScript logic changes plus two Handlebars template fixes) that resolves all six defects -- it performs the actual source-level fix an engineer would make, not a printed/echoed final answer or a direct write to a test-output file.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The task does not require the agent to produce any new output file for the tests to check; grading is done by rendering the agent's own existing templates and invoking existing TypeScript entry points in the cloned repo, so there is no file-reference requirement to document in instruction.md.
